# Pattern provenance and reference validation

`P01/manifest.json` pins the exact decoded regex, immutable source revision,
source settings, tokenizers 0.22.2 wheel hash, generated Unicode table hash, and
fixture hash. Ordinary Go tests are offline and verify these hashes.

Regenerate with the Python environment from `benchmark/prepare/requirements.txt`:

```sh
python generate.py
```

Run this command from this directory. The script performs no network access. It
reads the P01 manifest for provenance and the original P05 cases as shared input
seeds. It enumerates the pinned oracle's L|M class over every Unicode scalar,
then generates independent matches and isolated split spans for 26,820 cases:
word-class boundaries, exhaustive short strings, mixed scripts and punctuation,
contractions, whitespace, long runs, and the existing randomized Qwen inputs.
Python scalar offsets are converted to UTF-8 byte offsets before writing fixtures.

`internal/scan/word_tables.go` contains the precomputed L|M union needed by P01. N,
whitespace and contraction-fold tables are shared with P05. The template selects
the P05 L table or P01 L|M table once; both use the same ASCII path and a single
Unicode table lookup. See the [supported-pattern registry](../../docs/SupportedPatterns.md)
for all implemented expressions and tokenizer examples.

`P02/manifest.json` contains exact-pattern provenance and reference settings only.
P02 has no stored oracle arrays and is not generated by `generate.py`. The common
benchmark pipeline builds HF references in memory for every P02 request and checks
both matches and isolated splits. Ordinary Go tests include small inline HF cases
and differential fuzzing against Go regexp, which supports this ASCII expression.
The native-build guard reuses existing P05 fixtures with their own P05 expression;
that guard is separate from actual P02 compatibility verification.

`P04/manifest.json` pins the exact source expression and generated case-class
profile. `generate_case_tables.py` enumerates every Unicode scalar with HF
Tokenizers 0.22.2, creating disjoint `Lu|Lt`, `Ll`, and `Lm|Lo|M` ranges in
`internal/scan/case_tables.go`. It updates table/generator/wheel hashes, and does
not generate expected-output arrays:

```sh
python testdata/patterns/generate_case_tables.py
```

Run from the repository root with the pinned Python environment. Ordinary Go
tests verify the table/profile hashes and include inline HF regressions and a
separate greedy-backtracking model for candidate selection. Massive testing uses
live HF matches and splits on the shared corpus. Its inputs include exhaustive
class transitions, table-boundary neighbors, random mixes, and long runs. As with
P02, P04's native-build guard reuses existing P05 fixtures with the P05 regex;
actual P04 verification follows as a separate mandatory stage.

`P03/manifest.json` pins the source expression and its HF line-anchor semantics.
No output arrays are stored. Live references verify the shared corpus; offline
Go tests use an explicit copy of the pinned whitespace set and a multiline `$`
assertion. Go's default `$` and ASCII-only `\s` are not equivalent substitutes.
Long unsuccessful whitespace runs are tested through 1 Mi scalars in Go; the
common corpus includes shorter stress cases to keep the regex baseline tractable.
The native-build guard uses the existing P05 fixtures with their P05 expression.

`P09/manifest.json` and `P13/manifest.json` pin their exact strings, source revisions,
and source split settings. P09 contains literal CR/LF characters after JSON
unescaping; P13 uses factored contractions and possessive quantifiers. Both reuse
one immutable P05 scanner plan. Each runs its own live HF matches/splits gate on
all common requests and has separately keyed benchmark results. No new expected
output archive is stored. Existing P05 fixtures guard the reference binary using
the P05 expression; the subsequent live gate uses the selected alias expression.

`P16`, `P07`, `P24`, and `P20` contain provenance manifests only. They use the
same live HF pipeline and P05 native-build guard. The common corpus includes
mixed Nd/Nl/No runs, supplementary-plane numbers, bounded-run residues, and
endpoints plus neighbors of every pinned number range. Offline tests use inline
HF byte offsets and an independent Go regex over the pinned N class; fuzzing
checks numeric gaps/grouping as well as UTF-8 and partition invariants.

`P19` and `P06` contain source manifests only. They reuse the pinned P04 word
classes and contraction folds. Their live HF gate checks optional suffixes after
both ordered word alternatives, leading-mark backtracking, failed/partial and
repeated suffixes, scoped case folds, and numeric bounds. Inline HF regressions
and independent word-backtracking/suffix-regex fuzzing complement the shared
corpus gate; no expected-output archive is stored.

The P08/P11/P17/P18/P21/P23 directories contain only provenance manifests. Their exact literal sets, optional prefixes and complement semantics are validated by live HF references in the common benchmark pipeline. Ordinary offline tests include captured HF edge cases and independent RE2 comparisons over all valid Unicode scalars. No corpus output arrays are stored.

P12/P15 store provenance manifests only. Their reference matches and isolated splits are generated live. Offline tests compare ordered alternatives using RE2 with explicit pinned Hangul ranges, exercise group transitions and overlaps, and cover every valid scalar. Run `benchmark/prepare/grouped.py` with tokenizers==0.22.2 to verify Hangul extraction without storing oracle outputs.

P22 stores a provenance manifest and hashes of its reproducible P|S table generator, generated table and pinned HF native wheel. `generate_punctuation_tables.py` regenerates membership from all valid scalars with tokenizers==0.22.2; it stores no reference output arrays. The common native gate generates P22 matches and isolated splits live.

P10 stores source provenance and hashes of the pinned Nd table and its generator.
Run `python testdata/patterns/generate_decimal_tables.py` from the root with
tokenizers==0.22.2 to regenerate all 71 ranges. No output arrays are stored.
Offline tests compare captured HF boundaries and an independent RE2 whole-subject
expression with a captured prefix. The shared native gate checks exact anchors,
repeated triples, Nd membership and UTF-8 byte offsets with live references.
